header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rem:anonymous:m225:norm, from the Referenzkorpus Mittelhochdeutsch, ReM 2.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.1r.3: lûne is the day of the lunar month. At 1r.4 only the end of a word (-ene) survives before 'and', perhaps an adjective for the maiden. The last two lines (1v.1-2) are fragments.

nodes.text: will be good and friendly; the maiden
[...] and will not grow old; the sick person dies soon,
[or] lies ill a very long time. The dream comes true. The thirteenth
moon is good from midday on; but it is
not good for beginning anything. A child born [then]
becomes manly, bold and proud, and does not grow old;
the maiden becomes bold and proud, and dies soon;
the sick person soon gets well, or else he dies soon;
the dream comes to pass within seven days. The fourteenth moon
is good for all things. The child born becomes bold
[and] proud, and dies soon; the maiden becomes proud, unchaste
with men, and dies soon; the sick person recovers
soon, or he dies soon; the dream comes to pass soon.
The fifteenth moon is not good; an oath will
not hold. The child born will be good, and comes
into danger from iron or from water; the maiden becomes
chaste and lovable; the sick person dies if he
does not get well after two days; the dream does harm.
The sixteenth moon
[the] sick person dies
